name: How much does a garage conversion ADU cost in Los Angeles after all soft costs?

mainEntity.name: What is the real total cost of a garage conversion ADU in Los Angeles once design, permits, utility upgrades, and inspections are included?
mainEntity.text: What is the real total cost of a garage conversion ADU in Los Angeles once design, permits, utility upgrades, and inspections are included?

acceptedAnswer.text: A useful budget should separate hard costs from soft costs. Hard costs cover framing, finishes, plumbing, electrical, HVAC, insulation, windows, and bathrooms. Soft costs may include architectural drawings, structural engineering, permit processing, school or impact-related fees when applicable, survey work, title review, energy compliance, and consultant coordination. In older Los Angeles-area homes, the budget can rise further if the existing garage needs slab repair, seismic upgrades, drainage correction, fire-rated separation, or utility trenching. That is why a low per-square-foot estimate can be misleading. Homeowners should ask for a line-item estimate that shows allowances for design, permits, and contingency. A practical rule is to keep a reserve for unknowns because garage conversions often expose hidden issues only after demolition begins. The cheapest quote is not always the best one if it excludes utility upgrades or code corrections.
acceptedAnswer.description: Total cost is usually higher than construction-only quotes because garage conversions also include design, plan check, permit fees, utility coordination, engineering, and possible code upgrades. In Los Angeles-area projects, soft costs can materially change the budget, especially if the garage lacks adequate foundation, insulation, or sewer and electrical capacity.
